questions.def: 'Even though' shows contrast, even with rain.
questions.question: I want to go to the park ___ it is raining.

questions.def: 'As soon as' means immediately after arriving.
questions.question: She will call you ___ she arrives.

questions.def: 'Without' needs a gerund ('-ing' form).
questions.question: He left ___ goodbye.

questions.def: 'Because' introduces a reason or cause.
questions.question: ___ he studies hard, he gets good grades.

questions.def: 'If' introduces a condition.
questions.question: I will help you ___ I can.

questions.def: 'After' is followed by a gerund ('-ing' form).
questions.question: After ___ dinner, we went out.

questions.def: 'Because' gives the reason for not going to work.
questions.question: She didn't go to work ___ she was sick.

questions.def: 'Since' can mean 'because' (reason).
questions.question: ___ it was late, I decided to walk home.

questions.def: 'Will' is unneeded after 'unless' - use present simple: 'unless it rains'.
questions.question: Unless it will rain, we go to the beach.

questions.def: Beginning with gerund shows what happened first.
questions.question: ___ in London, I learned a lot.

questions.def: 'If' introduces a conditional clause.
questions.question: He will go ___ you go.

questions.def: 'Because' gives the reason for being tired.
questions.question: She is tired ___ she worked all day.

questions.def: 'After' is followed by a gerund ('-ing' form).
questions.question: After ___ my work, I went home.

questions.def: 'Although' introduces a contrast.
questions.question: ___ she is rich, she is not happy.

questions.def: 'If' introduces a conditional clause.
questions.question: She will be happy ___ you visit her.

questions.def: 'Before' needs a gerund ('-ing' form).
questions.question: Before ___ to school, I eat breakfast.

questions.def: 'If' introduces a condition for travelling.
questions.question: She will travel ___ she has the money.

questions.def: 'Until' means up to a certain time.
questions.question: He can't go out ___ he finishes his work.

questions.def: 'After' needs a gerund ('-ing' form).
questions.question: After ___ the book, I watched a film.

questions.def: 'When' indicates the time of the phone call.
questions.question: I will call you ___ I get home.

questions.def: 'Because' gives the reason she went to bed.
questions.question: She went to bed ___ she was tired.

questions.def: 'Before' needs a gerund ('-ing' form).
questions.question: Before ___, I always make coffee.

questions.def: 'Even though' shows contrast (like vs dislike).
questions.question: I like the dress ___ it is expensive.

questions.def: 'If' introduces a condition for her going.
questions.question: She will go ___ he goes.

questions.def: Use 'after' to show something happens later.
questions.question: I want to go to the party ___ I finish my homework.

questions.def: 'As soon as' indicates immediate action after arrival.
questions.question: She will call you ___ she arrives.

questions.def: 'After' needs past participle with 'have'.
questions.question: I will tell you ___ I have ___ dinner.

questions.def: 'So' shows the result of not studying.
questions.question: He didn't study, ___ he failed the test.

questions.def: 'If' introduces a condition.
questions.question: I will help you ___ you need it.

questions.def: 'Because' needs past simple to show reason.
questions.question: ___ he ___ hard, he passed the exam.
